Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of Petitioner no.1 and late Venkataravana.
3. That on 15.05.2022 at about 07.30 PM., the deceased Venaktaravana was moving on the left side of the road as a pedestrian, in front of Reddy watar station, Hirandahalli in Avalahalli road, wherein the driver of the two wheeler bearing Reg No.KA-27-H-3236, drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Venataravana and caused the accident.
In the 3 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 said accident Venkataravana sustained grievous injuries and he died on the spot due to the accidental injuries.
Later post mortem was conducted in East Point Hospital, the petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- for the same.
4. Petitioners alleged that prior to the accident deceased Venkataramana was hale and healthy and he was aged about 55 years and was working as a coolie and thereby he was earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
They stated that they are depending on the income of the deceased and he was the sole earning member of their family.
They further stated that the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Jurisdictional police have registered the Cri.No.180/2022 against the driver of the said vehicle.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he has not insured his vehicle and he is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.

5. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, he has not chosen to appear before this 4 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 tribunal to contest the petition and he placed exparte as per order dated 09.11.2023.
6.
In order to prove the case, Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1, produced and marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 13.
cross examination of PW-1 is taken as nil as respondent placed exparte.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments form the counsel appearing for petitioners and perused the entire records.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following points arise for my consideration :
:POINTS:-
1.Whether the Petitioners prove that, on 15- 05-2022 at about 07.30 p.m, the deceased was walking near Reddy water station road, Hirandahalli,
Bidarahalli - Avalahalli road, Bangalore district, at that time driver of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-27-H-3236 came in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life and dashed to the deceased, as a result of forced impact, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 5 SCCH-19  MVC.5363/2023  Issue no.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In partly affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Point No.1 & 2 :- I have taken both the issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and wife of the deceased Venkataravana, she has reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

11. In order to establish the actionable negligence petitioners have tender complaint, FIR, Mahazar,
IMV, Inquest, PM report, Final report which are at Ex.P.1 to 3, 5 to 8.

According to the petitioners,
the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the respondent who was driver of the offending vehicle and he has not insured his vehicle.

12. On careful perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Venkataravana was died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of respondent who was the driver and owner Ravanamma vs Subramani P M on 15 June, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6172378/
3 of the offending vehicle as on the date of incident.
Investigation officer has filed the final report as per Ex.P.8 against the respondent.
It is also true that respondent has not insured his vehicle accordingly investigation officer has invoked section 196 6 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 of IMV Act.

It is true that final report is filed after investigation and it is the substantial evidence and it cannot be doubted.
13.
The oral testimony of PW-1 and documents relied on by her remains unimpeached and unrebutted.
Petitioners have not tender the document to substantiate the occupation and income of the deceased as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly the prescribed notional income as on the date of accident as to be relied on.
Accident occurred on 15.05.2022, accordingly the monthly income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.15,500/- per month and admittedly he was married and self employed.

14. As per the Adhaar card of the deceased tender by the petitioners which is at Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the deceased was 01.01.1966 and deceased was 56 years age as on the date of the accident.
Accordingly the multiplier 9 is applicable.
15. Deceased was self employee and he was more than 50 years, accordingly 10% should be added towards his monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased left behind 3 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

16. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs. 15,500/-
Add: 10% of income future prospectus Rs. 1,550/-
Rs. 17,050/-
7 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 2 Less; 1/3rd for personal living expenses Rs. 5,683/- 4 Monthly income Rs. 11,367/-
Rs.11,367 (income)X 12 (month) X 9 Rs.12,27,636/- (Multiplier )
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.12,27,636/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
17. Loss of estate;

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.
18.

Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

19. Loss of Consortium :
Ravanamma vs Subramani P M on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6172378/
4
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

In this petition, the petitioners are the wife,
children of the deceased, accordingly they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/-
each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.40,000X3 = Rs.1,20,000/- as compensation under this head.
20. Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl No. Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency Rs.12,27,636/-
2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.13,77,636/-.

22. Rate of Interest: The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
23. Liability:
Admittedly respondent is the owner and driver of the offending vehicle and he has not insured his vehicle.
Accordingly respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount along interest.
Accordingly he is directed deposit the same before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Point no.1 in the affirmative and Point no.2, in partly affirmative.

9 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 24. Issue No.3; For the foregoing reasons and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:

5 ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.13,77,636/-with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till its realization.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for Rs.4,59,212/- each with interest.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1 to 3 are permitted to withdraw their respective share with interest through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020 Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.

Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed off.
10 SCCH-19 MVC.5363/2023 Draw award accordingly.
